verdict.rationale: Glama publishes a quality scoring system (TDQS) and a scanned/scored catalog (glama-probe-1: '90,845 servers... every one scanned, scored'; glama-docs-6, glama-docs-11 support search/compare with capability inspection; glama-docs-16 shows a verified-ownership badge mechanism), and one community member praises the TDQS scoring concept (glama-comm-1). However, hands-on reports directly contradict reliable functioning of this quality signal: a user's score wouldn't rerun for 3 days despite resyncs, traced to an undocumented credit-card requirement (glama-comm-2), and neither the user nor their AI agent could diagnose why the retest wasn't triggering after 4 days (glama-comm-3). This is a concrete operational failure of the very quality-signal feature being judged. Missing for 10: documented usage-count metrics, explicit liveness/health-check indicators, and independent confirmation that scores/badges update reliably without hidden paywalls.
